title: Odile and the Alibi
premise: Isandro Dravenmoor, a night-shift taxi dispatcher who has spent years making themselves unnoticeable, receives a strange prepaid request: a client wants a driver to shadow one Odile Vasseur and gather proof that her murder — scheduled, allegedly, for the winter solstice — will not happen. Digging in, Isandro discovers that Odile was declared dead two years ago, that the police file is sealed, and that everyone connected to the case insists it stay closed. As Isandro and Odile form an uneasy alliance of two people who survive by not being seen, they uncover a cover-up woven through the city's taxi commission, a missing witness, and a killer hiding inside Isandro's own dispatch office. In the end, Isandro must choose between returning to invisibility or testifying — and by stepping into the light, they finally find the belonging they never believed they could have.
about_author: Zephyrine Dunmore is the pen name of a former night dispatcher who spent eleven years listening to a city breathe through a headset before turning those voices into fiction. They write mysteries about people the world overlooks, and they still can't sleep before midnight.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On a slow Tuesday shift, an envelope arrives at the dispatch office: cash, a photo of a woman named Odile Vasseur, and instructions to confirm she is alive through the solstice. The emotional beat is wary curiosity — Isandro has seen every kind of fare, but never one paid to prevent a death.

chapters.title: A Woman Already Buried
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A records search reveals Odile Vasseur died two years ago; there's a death certificate, a closed case, a sealed file. Yet the woman in the photo walks past the depot every night at 2 a.m. The beat is vertigo — the ground of Isandro's ordered, invisible world tilting.

chapters.title: Two Years of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We learn why she let the city believe she died: fleeing an abusive partner with police connections, she vanished into the one job where no one looks at your face. Her beat is exhausted vigilance — freedom that feels like erasure.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Trying to trace the anonymous payer, Isandro finds the return address is a demolished building and the phone number belongs to a decommissioned cab. Someone with deep knowledge of the company set this up. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Fare Number Nine
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro begins assigning themselves Odile's route under pretext, riding along as her driver. Their first real conversation happens over a shared thermos in a parked cab. Beat: tentative connection between two professional nobodies.

chapters.title: What the Solstice Means
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile admits she received the same warning Isandro did — someone is telling them both a murder is coming. She suspects her 'widower,' Tomas Reyes, who inherited everything when she died. Beat: fear becoming strategy.

chapters.title: The Sealed File
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A sympathetic retired detective, Marisol Quintero, warns Isandro off: the original investigator on Odile's death case retired abruptly after the file was sealed from above. Beat: the mystery widens from a stalker story into institutional rot.

chapters.title: Night Crew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Introducing the depot's night crew — dispatcher Ren, mechanic Bo, and supervisor Halloran — the found family both leads orbit. Odile realizes Isandro isn't the only one watching her; someone else has been asking the crew questions too. Beat: warmth undercut by paranoia.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Following Odile home, Isandro spots a second tail — a gray sedan that vanishes near the taxi commission's impound lot. When Isandro runs the plate, it comes back registered to a car that was scrapped last year. Beat: the watcher is being watched.

chapters.title: Confessions at 4 A.M.
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs in a single long scene. Over diner coffee, Isandro and Odile trade their histories — why each chose invisibility, what it cost. Beat: intimacy; the alibi of the title becomes literal, as they agree to be each other's witnesses.

chapters.title: Halloran Knows Something
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Supervisor Halloran is caught shredding old dispatch logs covering the week Odile disappeared. He claims he's protecting the crew, not himself. Beat: betrayal inside the found family; trust becomes a currency running out.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Retired
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile tracks down the original case's key witness, a former commission clerk now living quietly upstate. The clerk confirms: Odile's 'death' was staged with help from inside the commission — and the person who arranged it is still employed there. Beat: the map redraws itself.

chapters.title: Ren's Alibi
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Evidence points toward fellow dispatcher Ren, whose schedule matches the gray sedan sightings. Confronting Ren, Isandro learns Ren was being blackmailed over an old DUI — forced to run errands for someone whose voice came through a burner phone. Beat: suspicion pivoting toward a hidden hand.

chapters.title: Tomas Reyes Cries Beautifully
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile confronts her 'widower,' who swears he mourns her and produces his own threatening notes — he's being framed as the fall guy. One of them is true: he says, the killer wants a body, and any body will do. Beat: the trap's shape becomes visible.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The prepaid contract's deadline is tomorrow. Isandro reconstructs the dispatch logs and finds the pattern: every 'errand' Ren ran traced back to a terminal in the dispatch office itself. The killer has been listening to the whole city through the same headset Isandro wears. Beat: cold horror.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile realizes the only person with access to that terminal, the blackmail material, and the sealed file is Halloran — who once worked the commission and whose 'protection' of the crew was really containment. She goes to warn Isandro. Beat: race against the clock.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro is lured to the impound lot by a fake emergency call and confronted by Halloran, who confesses: he staged Odile's death for money, and now that she's resurfaced, loose ends must be tied. The gray sedan arrives — Halloran wasn't working alone. Beat: cliffhanger peril.

chapters.title: What Odile Saw
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile, following Isandro's GPS ping, witnesses the ambush and makes the choice she's avoided for two years: she steps out of the shadows, calls 911, and uses her own name aloud for the first time since her 'death.' Beat: identity reclaimed at gunpoint.

chapters.title: The Second Passenger
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The accomplice is revealed — the retired detective Quintero's former partner, now a commission board member, who sealed the file to bury his own embezzlement trail. Halloran tries to flee in a cab; Isandro, using dispatcher authority, locks the fleet remotely and broadcasts his confession over the open channel. Beat: triumphant reversal using the tools of invisibility.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Arrests, statements, and the unraveling of the commission cover-up. Isandro must testify publicly — the ultimate end of anonymity — while Odile petitions to have her death certificate reversed. Beat: fear transmuted into courage; cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: Alive on Paper
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The certificate is voided; Odile legally exists again and grieves the ghost-self she must retire. The night crew throws her a terrible, wonderful party in the depot. Beat: bittersweet rebirth; belonging chosen, not defaulted into.

chapters.title: First Fare of the Morning
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, epilogue. Months later, Isandro takes a day shift for the first time — visible, named, known. A new envelope arrives on the desk: another impossible request. Isandro smiles, pockets it, and calls Odile. Beat: hopeful, open-ended — the invisible pair now work in the light, together.
